plan_summary: Install and configure Nginx on Ubuntu 24.04 by updating system packages, adding the official repository key if necessary, installing the package, verifying the service status, and configuring basic security defaults.
assumptions: The host has network connectivity to download packages.
The user has sudo privileges to install software.

tasks.title: Update system package lists and upgrade existing packages
tasks.objective: Ensure the local package index is current before installing new software.
tasks.rationale: Running apt update prevents installation of outdated versions and resolves dependency conflicts early in the process.
tasks.expected_output: Command completes with a summary of packages upgraded or no changes needed.
success_criteria: No critical errors reported during update

tasks.title: Verify Nginx repository availability or add official key
tasks.objective: Ensure the system can locate the latest Nginx packages for Ubuntu 24.04.
tasks.rationale: Ubuntu 24.04 may require adding a specific GPG key or repository source if not included by default in the main repo.
tasks.expected_output: Confirmation that the Nginx package is available via 'apt search nginx' or that the key was added successfully.
success_criteria: No GPG signature errors when attempting to install

tasks.title: Install Nginx package and dependencies
tasks.objective: Download and install the Nginx web server software.
tasks.rationale: This is the core installation step that places binaries, libraries, and configuration files onto the system.
tasks.expected_output: Nginx installed in /usr/sbin/nginx with default configuration in /etc/nginx.

tasks.title: Start and enable the Nginx service
tasks.objective: Launch the Nginx daemon and configure it to start on boot.
tasks.rationale: Installation alone does not run the server; systemd units must be started and enabled for persistence.
tasks.expected_output: Nginx process running in background, service status shows 'active (running)'.

tasks.title: Verify Nginx responds to HTTP requests
tasks.objective: Confirm the web server is functional and listening on port 80.
tasks.rationale: Functional verification ensures the installation was successful and the service is bound to the network interface.
tasks.expected_output: Browser or curl command returns the default 'Welcome to nginx!' page.

tasks.title: Review and secure default configuration files
tasks.objective: Inspect standard config files for security best practices.
tasks.rationale: Default configurations often lack SSL or specific security headers; reviewing them prevents immediate vulnerabilities.
tasks.expected_output: List of identified configuration sections requiring review (e.g., server_tokens, ssl settings).
success_criteria: No critical security misconfigurations found in defaults

tasks.title: Configure firewall rules for Nginx
tasks.objective: Allow incoming traffic on port 80 (and 443 if SSL is added later) via UFW.
tasks.rationale: Even with a running service, the host firewall must allow traffic to reach the web server.
tasks.expected_output: Port 80 allowed in firewall rules, Nginx profile applied if available.

tasks.title: Document installation steps and current state
tasks.objective: Create a brief record of the installation process for future reference.
tasks.rationale: Documentation aids in troubleshooting and ensures reproducibility if the system needs to be rebuilt.
tasks.expected_output: A text file containing commands run, versions installed, and current configuration paths.
success_criteria: File contains version numbers and key commands used
